explanation: The theorem says that complex multiplication by l, viewed as an ℝ-linear map ℂ → ℂ, has determinant ‖l‖^2. Mathlib has no single lemma stating this. The proof combines several Mathlib lemmas: LinearMap.det_restrictScalars (restricting scalars turns the determinant into Algebra.norm), ContinuousLinearMap.det_toSpanSingleton (a simp lemma), Algebra.norm_complex_eq (norm from ℂ to ℝ equals normSq) and Complex.normSq_eq_norm_sq. The closest single candidate is Algebra.norm_complex_apply (Algebra.norm ℝ z = normSq z, where Algebra.norm is by definition det ∘ lmul). Using it would still require an ext/mul_comm step identifying D l with lmul ℝ ℂ l, plus Algebra.norm_apply and normSq_eq_norm_sq, which is more than routine glue. Mathlib's own UpperHalfPlane.det_smulFDeriv is proved with the same simp set, so Mathlib has no packaged lemma for this. Searched: det lemmas in Analysis/Complex, RingTheory/Complex.lean and Topology/Algebra/Module/Determinant.lean; name guesses det_lmul, det_mulLeft, det_lsmul, det_restrictScalars and det_toSpanSingleton; and det together with normSq.
